title: Kanban: a reference swimlane heading ignores the target object's declared nameField, so swimlane and column-lane headings can name the same record differently
body:
triage#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbZKP5YM48rWMWTS7wE

Filing gate: ① an experience defect, filed by triage at repo:objectstack#3's request (mailbox #36743, comment 7127703645). Source: a follow-up from PR #36925 (#36841, kanban swimlanes keyed by reference id).

Blocked-by: #36925

## What happens

After PR #36925, a kanban board whose swimlanes group by a lookup field titles each swimlane with the referenced record's title. That title does not read the target object's declared `nameField`. A column lane over the same reference does read it, so the same record can be named differently in a swimlane heading and in a column heading on one board.

reach: boards that group swimlanes by a lookup to an object whose `nameField` is not its default title field.

## Expected

Swimlane headings name a referenced record the same way column-lane headings do, through the target object's `nameField`.

## Acceptance

- `ObjectKanban` reads the swimlane field's target object schema once per board (`useSettledSchema`) and passes it down through `KanbanBoardCore`, `index.tsx` and `KanbanImpl`. This is the dev's sizing: S.
- A test pins a swimlane over a lookup whose target declares a non-default `nameField`: the heading shows that field, and it matches the column-lane heading for the same record.

Dedupe: open issues for swimlane headings and `nameField` return only #36841, the parent that #36925 fixes.
